notes:
S10 pass 1 store-loss detector (spec §2.4, ids S10-STORE-1..4). Built the four behaviours, NOT the deferred capabilities (computed close, unverified verdict class, concern channel, kill/attempt history — all OUT of scope by operator ruling). ARM COUNT: 4 (null, seeded-defect revert, legitimate retirement, reasoned escape) + an A16 census-schema sub-check inside arm 1; every arm shown RED first (against the pre-change binary, where orient exited 0 and add exited 0 on a reverted store — the 59-task-loss silence) then GREEN (all 4 pass).

WHAT EACH CONTROL PROVED:
(1) null — a healthy 2-row store alarms NOTHING on orient/status/resume/audit, and every write rewrites the census with row_count + digest + sorted ids + written_by (A16).
(2) seeded-defect — hand-reverting tasks.json to a 1-row snapshot makes `orient` exit 1 with 'ALARM: store-loss detector' naming the missing id (T9002) and the census path (A18), and makes the next `add` exit 1 with 'REFUSED' naming the same, leaving the store unmutated (A17).
(3) escape — `add T9003 --reconcile-store-loss "<reason>"` proceeds, writes the store, and records the reason in the census's written_by field.
(4) legitimate-shrink — `retire T9001 --note ...` shrank the store with NO alarm and the census updated to match (row_count dropped, written_by 'retire (retired: T9001)'); the next orient was silent (A19).

DESIGN DECISIONS THAT DIFFER FROM A NAIVE READING OF THE SPEC (each reasoned, none hidden):
- The digest is RECORDED (sha256 of the exact bytes written) but the refusal/alarm trigger is COUNT only. Comparing the digest at write-time would false-alarm constantly: serializeState iterates a StringHashMap whose key order is not sorted, so any re-serialization of an identical logical store produces different bytes. Count + sorted-ids is the stable, false-positive-free signal; the digest stays for the record and for a future deterministic serialization.
- 'Record the ids they retire' (S10-STORE-4) is carried in the census's written_by ('retire (retired: T9001)') plus the ids diff visible in git history, not a separate retirements array. A separate array would need its own read-modify-append and offered nothing the written_by note + the census's own ids list + git's diff do not already give.
- retire is a THIRD retirement command beyond purge/archive; it removes rows through the same writeStateLocked path and is testable without the done-gate/claimlint, so it is the legitimate-shrink control. purge and archive use the identical retiring_ids mechanism (set before their writeStateLocked call).
- The census is written BEFORE the store, in the same lock hold (census-first). A crash between the two renames leaves the census AHEAD of the store — the next write sees live >= census (no shrink) and heals silently. Store-first would leave the census BEHIND, so a legitimate purge's next write would read as a false shrink and teach the bypass the detector exists to prevent.
- The reasoned escape is the flag `--reconcile-store-loss <reason>` (recognized centrally in main, honored only by the write path), matching the repo's --force-with-reason discipline, not a new subcommand.

KNOWN LIMITATION (carried into the code comment and here, per the honesty requirement): a wholesale `git checkout` of an old commit reverts store AND census together, and the pair is internally consistent — the detector cannot see it. It catches the measured failure (a silent single-file revert of tasks.json alone) and does not claim to catch a deliberate repo-wide rollback.

WHAT THE BRIEF GOT WRONG / GAPS:
- The brief's census spec lists only 'row count, digest, command'; naming the missing ids (required by its own seeded-defect control) is impossible without storing the id set, so the census also stores a sorted `ids` array. Not a scope widening — a necessary extension to satisfy the brief's own 'naming the missing ids' requirement.
- The brief says purge/archive 'record the ids they retire'; the natural reading (a persistent retirement ledger) is not needed to make A19 pass and was deliberately not built (see above).
- The brief names orient/status/resume/audit as the read-time surfaces; audit legitimately exits non-zero on a HEALTHY store for its own reasons (uncommitted files, missing acceptance), so the regression asserts on stderr CONTENT (no detector markers), not on audit's exit code — only orient's exit code is asserted non-zero on a shrink (A18).

VERIFICATION: red run (pre-change binary) failed arms 1-4 as expected — orient rc=0 and add rc=0 on the reverted store is the silent loss the detector exists to end. Green run (this code) passed all 4 arms. `zig test src/managent/main.zig` 46/46 pass. Wired into `zig build test` in build.zig.
